lesson.title: Gender Heuristics & Suffix Clues
lesson.subtitle: Decode gender instead of memorizing: -ung is feminine, -chen is neuter, -er is masculine

hook.title: The Suffix Tells You
hook.content: You were told gender is arbitrary. Mostly false: German gender is written on the word's tail. Endings in -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -ion are feminine — die Wahrnehmung (perception), die Zeitung (newspaper, 'a timing'). -chen and -lein are neuter, no exceptions — das Mädchen ('the little girl', the famous paradox). Nouns built from verbs with -er are masculine — der Staubsauger, the dust-sucker. Most plain -e nouns are feminine — die Straße, die Woche, die Lampe. Learn a dozen suffix laws and you can guess the gender of thousands of words you have never seen.

footnotes.title: Das Mädchen, the Famous Paradox
footnotes.content: Mädchen ('little maid') ends in the diminutive -chen, and -chen words are ALWAYS neuter — so the girl is grammatically an 'it'. The suffix outranks the sex: die Magd + chen → das Mädchen. The same law makes das Fräulein neuter.

pattern.title: The Suffix Court
pattern.content: Feminine squad: -ung (die Zeitung, die Wahrnehmung — built from verbs!), -heit, -keit (die Gesundheit — health), -schaft (die Wissenschaft — knowledge-ship, science), -ion (die Nation), and most -e (die Straße, die Woche, die Lampe). Masculine squad: -er from verbs (der Sauger, der Fernseher), -ling (der Zwilling!), -ismus (der Tourismus). Neuter squad: -chen, -lein (das Mädchen, das Fräulein), and all -zeug words (das Feuerzeug — the -zeug law you know from the compounds). Collect the suffixes and every new word arrives pre-gendered.
pattern.linguist_note: These suffixes are the app's compendium in miniature: Wahrnehmung is the calque of Latin perceptio (truth-taking), Begriff the calque of conceptus (by-grip) — the abstract suffixes rode in with the Latin calques and kept their gender accordingly.

exercises.prompt: Look past noun endings: which pair has a different connection?
exercises.meaning: Recognize a familiar German word by choosing between earlier connection patterns.
exercises.explanation: Two, better and what use T → S/SS/Z. Speak → sprechen uses K → CH.

exercises.prompt: Run the factory: build the -ung noun from 'warnen' (the act of warning):
exercises.explanation: warnen → Warnung: chop the verb's -en, glue -ung, collect the feminine article for free.

exercises.prompt: The famous paradox: why is 'das Mädchen' (the girl) neuter?
options: It is a spelling mistake that stuck
The suffix -chen is ALWAYS neuter — it outranks the meaning
exercises.target_answer: The suffix -chen is ALWAYS neuter — it outranks the meaning
exercises.meaning: The -chen law beats the sex of the referent
exercises.explanation: die Magd + -chen → das Mädchen. Suffix laws are the one place German gender is perfectly predictable — das Flugzeug obeys -zeug, and der Geburtstag carries Tag's masculine law into the compound.

exercises.prompt: Match each suffix with its gender law. Then recall earlier vocabulary in the short phrases:
exercises.target_answer: feminine — die Zeitung, neuter — das Mädchen, masculine — der Staubsauger, feminine — die Straße, die Briefmarke, ein Zahn, Wir können feiern und singen, das Flugzeug, die Wahrnehmung, der Begriff, mein Heimweh
exercises.meaning: -ung; -chen; -er agent nouns; plain -e (mostly); a tooth; We can celebrate and sing; the aeroplane; perception; the concept; my homesickness
exercises.explanation: Four laws cover thousands of nouns — guess first, verify later.

exercises.idea: you're describing your morning scene: the woman reads the newspaper
cues: Two feminine flags on show: die Frau (plain -e law) and die Zeitung (-ung factory) — and lesen mutates: sie liest

vocab_hints.note: lesen → er liest — the vowel mutates like geben → gibt
Zeit + ung — 'a timing' — built by the feminine -ung factory

exercises.explanation: Two feminine flags in one sentence: die Frau (plain -e law) and die Zeitung (-ung law).

summary.outcome: Predict gender from suffixes: -ung/-heit/-e feminine, -chen neuter, -er/-ling masculine.
summary.takeaway: Gender is written on the tail: learn the suffix court and new nouns arrive pre-gendered.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Next: the feminine squad — -ung, -heit, -keit drills: derive abstract nouns and their genders.

twist.prompt: She quit the news: negate the noun — the woman reads the newspaper becomes the woman reads NO newspaper. (The -ung law still holds.)
twist.explanation: Zeitung is feminine (-ung law), so kein takes its feminine dress: keine. The suffix decided the gender — and the negation followed it.

wahrnehmung.etymology_derivation: Calque of Latin perceptio (wahr = true + nehmen = take → taking as true).

begriff.etymology_derivation: Calque of Latin conceptus (con- + capere → be- + greifen/Griff = grasp together).

zeit.etymology_derivation: t → z [ts] (cognate with English "tide", as in Yuletide or time and tide).

woche.context_phrase: Nächste Woche fahre ich nach Berlin.
woche.context_translation: Next week I travel to Berlin.

straße.etymology_derivation: Roman paved road (via strata) gave English "street" (kept Latin "t") and German "Straße" (shifted "t" to sharp "ß").

tochter.context_phrase: Meine Tochter lernt in der Schule.
tochter.etymology_derivation: Double shift: d → t and gh → ch.

butter.etymology_derivation: Borrowed together into West Germanic from Latin butyrum / Greek boutyron.

warnen.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *warnōn — a parallel formation to English warn (Old English wearnian). [wiktionary]

zeitung.context_phrase: Er liest jeden Morgen die Zeitung.
zeitung.context_translation: He reads the newspaper every morning.
zeitung.etymology_derivation: From Proto-West Germanic *tidungu, a message on the time-root — the page lists English tiding as the cognate: a Zeitung brings your tidings. [wiktionary]

berg.context_phrase: Der Berg ist im Winter weiß.
berg.context_translation: The mountain is white in winter.
berg.etymology_derivation: From Old High German bërg, from Proto-West Germanic *berg, from Proto-Germanic *bergaz. English barrow, a burial hill, is the listed cognate. [wiktionary]

geburtstag.etymology_derivation: Geburt + Tag, exactly English birthday; the Tag/day pair shows the d to t stop shift, and Geburt comes from the gebären family. [wiktionary]

feiern.context_translation: We are celebrating a birthday today.
feiern.etymology_derivation: From Old High German firOn, from fira, from Latin feriae (festival days) - the same Latin word that became the English fair, a market held on feast days. [wiktionary][etymonline]

flugzeug.etymology_derivation: Flug (flight, from fliegen — English fly) + Zeug (gear, as in Feuerzeug): the fly-gear. [wiktionary]

briefmarke.etymology_derivation: Brief (the twin of brief, both from Latin brevis, short) + Marke (the twin of mark, both from Germanic mark-, sign) — a letter-mark, that is, a postage stamp. [wiktionary]

vermissen.etymology_derivation: ver + missen (to miss): to miss through and through — the missen root pairs with English miss. [wiktionary]

handtasche.etymology_derivation: Hand + Tasche — the exact compound calque of handbag; both elements are documented twins. [wiktionary]
